 <section class="pp-target-segments">
 <h2 class="pp-headline">What complaints can the SaltDome help with?</h2>
 <div class="pp-accordion">
 <div class="pp-accordion-item">
 <input type="checkbox" id="pp_acc_1" class="pp-accordion-checkbox">
 <label for="pp_acc_1" class="pp-accordion-label">
 <span class="pp-accordion-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/nathas-allergias-no.png" alt="allergy" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;">
 </span>Respiratory allergy, hay fever<span class="pp-accordion-arrow"></span>
 </label>
 <div class="pp-accordion-content">
 <p>Salty air may help clear nasal passages and reduce mucosal swelling. Many allergy sufferers report milder symptoms when they start regular use 2–4 weeks before the season. Details: <a href="/hay-fever-salt-therapy">Hay fever and salt therapy</a>.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-accordion-item">
 <input type="checkbox" id="pp_acc_2" class="pp-accordion-checkbox">
 <label for="pp_acc_2" class="pp-accordion-label">
 <span class="pp-accordion-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/nathas-kisfiu.png" alt="common cold, child" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;">
 </span>Frequently ill children, recurrent colds<span class="pp-accordion-arrow"></span>
 </label>
 <div class="pp-accordion-content">
 <p>The mucolytic effect can aid faster recovery, and regular use may help prevent infections — valuable in preschool and school settings where illnesses spread quickly.<sup>7</sup> Details: <a href="/common-cold-and-salt-therapy">Cold and salt therapy</a>.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-accordion-item">
 <input type="checkbox" id="pp_acc_3" class="pp-accordion-checkbox">
 <label for="pp_acc_3" class="pp-accordion-label">
 <span class="pp-accordion-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/tusszento-arc.png" alt="asthma" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;">
 </span>Asthma — as an adjunct treatment<span class="pp-accordion-arrow"></span>
 </label>
 <div class="pp-accordion-content">
 <p>Research suggests salt therapy may have favourable adjunctive effects in asthma without side effects — also in children.<sup>3,6</sup> Important: in an asthma attack it does NOT replace your rescue inhaler! Details: <a href="/asthma-halotherapy">Asthma and salt therapy</a>.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-accordion-item">
 <input type="checkbox" id="pp_acc_4" class="pp-accordion-checkbox">
 <label for="pp_acc_4" class="pp-accordion-label">
 <span class="pp-accordion-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/tudo.png" alt="COPD" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;">
 </span>COPD and chronic respiratory diseases<span class="pp-accordion-arrow"></span>
 </label>
 <div class="pp-accordion-content">
 <p>Salty air can help loosen secretions and ease breathing; studies report improvements in lung function and quality of life — as a complement to medication, never a replacement.<sup>2,4,5</sup> Details: <a href="/copd-and-salt-therapy">COPD and salt therapy</a>.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-accordion-item">
 <input type="checkbox" id="pp_acc_5" class="pp-accordion-checkbox">
 <label for="pp_acc_5" class="pp-accordion-label">
 <span class="pp-accordion-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/arcureg-gyulladas.png" alt="sinusitis" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;">
 </span>Sinusitis, nasal congestion, snoring<span class="pp-accordion-arrow"></span>
 </label>
 <div class="pp-accordion-content">
 <p>The fine salt particles can reach the sinuses, helping to dissolve and remove secretions. If snoring is nasal in origin (caused by congestion or allergy), restoring free nasal breathing can reduce snoring. Details: <a href="/sinusitis-salt-therapy">Sinusitis and salt therapy</a>, <a href="/snoring-and-salt-therapy">Snoring and salt therapy</a>.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-accordion-item">
 <input type="checkbox" id="pp_acc_6" class="pp-accordion-checkbox">
 <label for="pp_acc_6" class="pp-accordion-label">
 <span class="pp-accordion-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/futo-no.png" alt="athlete" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;">
 </span>Athletes — exercise-induced asthma<span class="pp-accordion-arrow"></span></label>
 <div class="pp-accordion-content">
 <p>In athletes salty air may reduce exercise-induced asthma symptoms and support recovery. Details: <a href="/salt-therapy-for-athletes">Salt therapy for athletes</a>.</p>

 </div>

 <div class="pp-accordion-content">

 </div>
 </div>
 </div>
 <p>If you’re looking for the scientific background, history, and a detailed comparison of methods (salt cave, salt room, salt pipe, salt lamp), see the <a href="/salt-therapy-halotherapy-guide">Comprehensive salt therapy guide</a>.</p>
 </section>
 <!-- 5. HATÁSMECHANIZMUS – tömörítve, a részletek a pillar-cikkben -->
 <section>
 <h2 class="pp-headline">How does inhaled salty air work?</h2>
 <p>The SaltDome nebulizes saline ultrasonically, releasing 2–5 micron salt particles into the air. This size, research suggests, can reach the lower airways — small enough to reach the bronchi yet large enough to deposit there.<sup>8</sup> Salt that adheres to the mucosa can act in three ways:</p>
 <ul>
 <li><strong>Mucus thinning:</strong> salt’s osmotic effect draws water to the mucosal surface — like salting cucumber slices. Secretions thin and become easier to cough up and clear.<sup>8</sup></li>
 <li><strong>Mucosal calming:</strong> salt particles may reduce mucus viscosity and help restore normal mucosal function, which can be beneficial in allergic conditions.<sup>1,8</sup></li>
 <li><strong>Support for ciliary function:</strong> the tiny cilia that sweep mucus and debris outward can be reactivated; in chronic airway disease this function slows down, and salt therapy may aid its recovery.<sup>2</sup></li>
 </ul>
 </section>
 <!-- 7. FAQ – RADIO BUTTON (NINCS MIKRODATA) -->
 <section class="pp-faq-section">
 <h2 class="pp-headline">Frequently asked questions</h2>

 <div class="pp-faq-item">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_1" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_1" class="pp-faq-label">
 How long until I can expect results?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>Most users notice changes after a few days of regular nightly use. Salt therapy is not an acute treatment: consistency matters more than intensity. Give your body a few weeks before judging.</p>
 </div>
 </div>

 <div class="pp-faq-item">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_2" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_2" class="pp-faq-label">
 Is it safe for children?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>Yes, salt therapy is safe for children (consider that billions of people live by the seaside). Research in children found no adverse effects, and regular use may reduce upper respiratory infections.<sup>3,7</sup> Start 2–3 weeks before allergy season or kindergarten start.</p>
 </div>
 </div>

 <div class="pp-faq-item">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_3" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_3" class="pp-faq-label">
 How is the SaltDome different from a salt pipe or salt lamp?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>Salt pipes deliver coarse salt particles only to the upper airways, mainly affecting the mouth and throat. Salt lamps are decorative and do not emit therapeutic salt particles. The SaltDome’s ultrasonic nebulization produces 2–5 micron particles that can reach the lower airways — and when used nightly during sleep, regular use requires no extra time or willpower.</p>
 </div>
 </div>

 <div class="pp-faq-item">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_4" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_4" class="pp-faq-label">
 Which salt should I use, and how much does it consume?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>We recommend only additive-free, natural rock salt — iodized table salt or salt treated with anti-caking agents is not suitable for the airways. The <a href="/rock-salt">rock salt available in our shop</a> is optimised for the device. Consumption is minimal: one container lasts months with daily use.</p>
 </div>
 </div>

 <div class="pp-faq-item">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_5" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_5" class="pp-faq-label">
 How long and how often can it be used?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>There’s no rule that salt therapy must be limited to a few weeks — think of the millions who live by the sea. Adjust use to your family’s needs: during cold seasons (autumn–spring, school start) you can use it continuously for 2–3 months; start 2 weeks before allergy season.</p>
 </div>
 </div>

 <div class="pp-faq-item pp-faq-warning">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_6" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_6" class="pp-faq-label pp-faq-label-warning pp-faq-label-with-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/figyelmeztetes.png" alt="warning" style="height:20px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;margin-right:5px;">
 Can it replace medical treatment?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>No. Salt therapy is a complementary method to be used alongside medical treatment, not instead of it. If you have COPD, continue taking your prescribed medications; if you have asthma, keep your rescue inhaler at hand. Salt therapy aims to support natural defenses and improve quality of life.</p>
 </div>
 </div>

 <div class="pp-faq-item pp-faq-danger">
 <input type="radio" name="pp_faq" id="pp_faq_7" class="pp-faq-radio">
 <label for="pp_faq_7" class="pp-faq-label pp-faq-label-danger pp-faq-label-with-icon">
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/tiltas.png" alt="important" style="height:20px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;margin-right:5px;">
 Can I use it during an asthma attack?
 </label>
 <div class="pp-faq-body">
 <p>NO. In an asthma attack, use your rescue inhaler — salt therapy is for prevention and supporting symptom-free periods. Also wait until fever has subsided before using during acute respiratory infections.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 </section>

 <section class="pp-how-it-works">
 <h2 class="pp-headline">How to use the SaltDome?</h2>
 <div class="pp-steps-container">
 <div class="pp-step">
 <span class="pp-step-number">1</span>
 <div class="pp-step-content">
 <h3>Prepare the saline</h3>
 <p>Fill the tank with water and dissolve one measuring scoop of natural rock salt according to the user manual. The device produces 2–5 micron particles by ultrasonic nebulization.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-step">
 <span class="pp-step-number">2</span>
 <div class="pp-step-content">
 <h3>Place it near your bed</h3>
 <p>Put the device on a stable surface not far from your sleeping area. It affects roughly one bedroom’s airspace. Most effective when operating about one to one-and-a-half metres from your head.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-step">
 <span class="pp-step-number">3</span>
 <div class="pp-step-content">
 <h3>Turn it on — you can use the remote</h3>
 <p>Start it before falling asleep; you can control the mood-LED colour and operation from bed with the remote.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-step">
 <span class="pp-step-number">4</span>
 <div class="pp-step-content">
 <h3>Sleep — the device works</h3>
 <p>Daily night use of 6–8 hours is recommended: you’ll inhale gently salty air all night, unnoticed. During cold seasons you can also use it during the day for shorter periods.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 <div class="pp-step">
 <span class="pp-step-number">5</span>
 <div class="pp-step-content">
 <h3>Maintain it</h3>
 <p>Replace the saline regularly and clean the tank according to the manufacturer’s instructions — hygiene and proper maintenance are required for effective operation.</p>
 </div>
 </div>
 </div>
 </section>

 <!-- 12. ELLENJAVALLATOK – MedicalDevice MIKRODATA -->
 <section class="pp-contraindication-list">
 <h3>
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/tiltas.png" alt="warning" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;margin-right:5px;">
 When NOT to use the device
 </h3>
 <ul>
 <li>
 Active tuberculosis
 </li>
 <li>
 Airway bleeding
 </li>
 <li>
 Severe heart failure
 </li>
 <li>
 Acute respiratory infection with high fever – wait until the fever subsides
 </li>
 <li>
 Untreated, severe high blood pressure – consult your physician first
 </li>
 <li>
 Kidney disease – consult due to possible salt metabolism issues
 </li>
 <li>
 Malignant tumour – discuss with your treating physician beforehand
 </li>
 </ul>
 <p><strong>Unsure?</strong> If you have a chronic condition, consult your treating physician before starting salt therapy!</p>
 </section>

 <!-- 13. ORVOSI FIGYELMEZTETÉS – NEM MIKRODATA -->
 <section class="pp-medical-warning">
 <h3>
 <img src="https://shop.unas.hu/shop_ordered/21500/pic/emotic/professzor.png" alt="information" style="height:32px;width:auto;vertical-align:middle;margin-right:5px;">
 Important information
 </h3>
 <p>Salt therapy is a complementary treatment used alongside medical care, not instead of it. You may experience a temporary increase in coughing at the start — a sign of mucus clearance — and mild throat irritation in the first sessions. If symptoms persist or worsen, reduce session time or pause use and consult a physician.
 </p>
 <p class="pp-disclaimer"><em>The information here is for guidance only. Salt therapy is a complementary method and does not replace medical treatment. Consult your treating physician for complaints. Refer to the user manual for correct device use.</em></p>
 </section>
